_doc: PRE-REGISTERED spec for Phase 1 of the context-enrichment program (J 2026-07-14: 'do we cross-correlate any information before acting on signals... maybe it should be calculated beforehand and tagged onto the signal'). Phase 0 (commit b1597a6) shipped setup/scripts/context_bundle_producer.py::compute_trend_alignment -- a PURE, as-of-bounded function that reads daily/hourly/15m SPY structure and returns an alignment_score in [-3,+3], tagged onto the decision row LOGGED-ONLY (zero behavior change; nothing on the live decision path reads it yet). Phase 1 answers the actual question before anything is allowed to consume the tag: does trend alignment separate winning trades from losing trades? FROZEN BEFORE any scoring run -- exploratory != confirmatory, no re-picks after seeing results, a flat/non-monotonic KILL is a publishable outcome exactly like every other pre-reg in this program.
build_step_complete: compute_trend_alignment imported UNMODIFIED from context_bundle_producer (identity-pinned by test_trend_alignment_correlation_study.py::test_compute_trend_alignment_is_the_same_object). alignment_for_decision() is the ONE slicing boundary this module adds, guarded by 3 no-look-ahead tests. Fetch/cache infrastructure (fetch_historical_bars, paginated Alpaca REST) built and VERIFIED against live data at freeze time: daily=510 bars/1 page, hourly=4239 bars/20 pages, m15=14973 bars/20 pages, cached under analysis/backtests/cache/trend-alignment-spy-{tf}-2024-07-01_2026-07-14.json (NOT committed to git -- regenerable working cache, same convention as context-bundle.json; regenerate via `--build-cache --refresh`). Population loaders (load_p1_population/load_p2_population/load_p3_population) built and smoke-tested against real on-disk data, schema-pinned by test_trend_alignment_correlation_study.py.
hypothesis: Signals ALIGNED with the multi-timeframe (daily+hourly+15m) trend at entry have higher expectancy than signals FIGHTING it. Operationalized as: per-trade P&L, grouped by an AGREEMENT bucket in [-3..+3] (positive = trend agrees with the trade's own side, negative = trend fights it, computed via alignment_vs_side()'s signed_score -- NOT the raw market-direction alignment_score, so bull and bear populations pool onto the same agreement axis), should show monotonic-ish increasing expectancy from bucket -3 to +3, and losing episodes should skew toward negative buckets while winners skew toward positive buckets.
population_correction_disclosure: The task brief that spawned this study described P1 as 'n in thousands -- the population the ribbon_ride/exit studies use; find it'. Having searched (STRATEGY-SPACE-REGISTRY.jsonl, mass-grind-total.json, every backtest/tools/*_exit_matrix.py / *_ab.py script), the actual canonical strike-independent ribbon_ride signal cohort every exit/strike study in this repo reuses (T3/T4, ribbon_ride_strike_exit_ab.py, WP5-STRIKE-AB) is analysis/exit-parity/signal-set.json via _signal_cache.load_or_build_signals() -- n=250, not thousands. There is no larger canonical population with SS-B-replayed real-OPRA outcomes in this repo as of 2026-07-14. This pre-registration uses the REAL n=250 cohort and states that correction explicitly (OP-33: verify, don't inherit an unverified premise) rather than silently proceeding on a wrong assumption or fabricating a bigger population.

P1_large_historical_signal_population.label: MODELED
P1_large_historical_signal_population.window: 2025-01-01..2026-06-18 (both directions, L2 gate, cap OFF, OTM-2 signal-generating strike, BS_FALLBACK excluded -- real OPRA fills only per C1).
P1_large_historical_signal_population.outcome_method: DEFERRED TO SCORING RUN (not built/run in this commit -- the OPRA-heavy replay itself is the 'scoring' the task brief forbids this commit from running). When scored: reuse ribbon_ride_strike_exit_ab.py's load_cohort()/replay_cell() UNMODIFIED at strike='OTM-2' (CONTROL_STRIKE, matches the signal-generating strike so no strike-mismatch confound), shape=SS-B (structure_stop_study.SS_B_SHAPE, current live exit shape), use_structure=True, fill-bar convention '>' (PRIMARY per that script's own disclosed audit). QTY=10 fixed (repo research-scale convention). Real OPRA local cache via lib.option_pricing_real.load_contract_bars -- zero synthetic pricing.
P1_large_historical_signal_population.alignment_reconstruction: For each signal's entry_ts (naive ET), call trend_alignment_correlation_study.alignment_for_decision(daily_df, hourly_df, m15_df, entry_ts) against the cached full-history bars (fetch_historical_bars per timeframe), then alignment_vs_side(alignment, signal['direction']) for the signed agreement bucket. Zero look-ahead: alignment_for_decision slices every timeframe to <=entry_ts before calling compute_trend_alignment.

P2_real_engine_fills.label: MEASURED
P2_real_engine_fills.source: automation/state/fills-ledger.jsonl (broker-truth, broker_fills.py's pull from Alpaca /v2/account/activities/FILL), reconstructed into per-EPISODE rows via exit_shape_parity_study.reconstruct_positions() -- the SAME C31-safe grouping trade_autopsy.py and the 2026-07-11 ledger-forensics report use (never per-leg/per-order).
P2_real_engine_fills.n_verified_note: 113 = option-only (is_option==True) positions across ALL arms as of 2026-07-14 (fetch verified live during this build step). This supersedes the task brief's '~100, ledger-forensics window' (that report's window was 2026-06-26..2026-07-09, n=109-112 engine-attributed episodes) -- the ledger has grown by a few more trading days since. Scoring will report both the full n=113 and the engine-attributed-only subset.
P2_real_engine_fills.attribution_filter: Each raw fill row in fills-ledger.jsonl already carries an 'attribution' field ('engine'/'manual') -- unlike reconstruct_positions()'s own output (which drops it), attribution for a position is taken from its ENTRY fill(s)' attribution (matches the 2026-07-11 ledger-forensics report's convention: attribution of the entry decision, not the exit fill). The one known ambiguous episode that report flagged (safe-2 SPY260626P00732000, entry engine / exit fill untagged) is carried forward with the SAME resolution (counted as engine) -- not re-litigated here.
P2_real_engine_fills.exclusions: is_crypto==True fills excluded (crypto is gym-only, never a trading population per CLAUDE.md scope lock). Manual-attributed episodes are reported as a SEPARATE row, never pooled into the engine population's expectancy-by-bucket table.
P2_real_engine_fills.alignment_reconstruction: Same alignment_for_decision() call as P1, using each position's entry_ts_utc (already UTC, no naive-ET normalization needed) and direction derived from the entry symbol's option type via side_from_option_char().

P3_j_op16_source_of_truth.label: MODELED
P3_j_op16_source_of_truth.source: ssb_certification_study.J_ANCHOR_TRADES, reused VERBATIM via trend_alignment_correlation_study.load_p3_population() -- the SAME transcription CLAUDE.md OP-16 and the SS-B certification study already use (winner-sum-asserted == $1,542 in that module; re-asserted here by test_load_p3_population_is_the_op16_anchor_set).
P3_j_op16_source_of_truth.outcome_used_for_scoring: j_pnl (J's OWN real dollar outcome) is the primary label for these 7 -- NOT a fresh SS-B replay (these are real J fills, already MEASURED, not MODELED -- 'MODELED' above refers only to the alignment reconstruction step, which necessarily replays the market-structure read since no live context-bundle existed at trade time in April/May 2026, Phase 0 shipped 2026-07-14).
P3_j_op16_source_of_truth.alignment_reconstruction: Same alignment_for_decision() call, entry_ts built from date + entry_time_et (naive ET, normalized inside alignment_for_decision), direction via side_from_option_char(side).

primary_metric.statement: Expectancy (mean per-trade P&L) by AGREEMENT bucket (signed_score in [-3..+3], from alignment_vs_side), computed SEPARATELY per population (P1/P2/P3 never pooled -- different label types, different n, different eras) and then as a POOLED cross-population check using only the sign/direction of the relationship (not raw dollars, which are not comparable across QTY=10-research-scale P1 vs real-account-sized P2/P3).
primary_metric.winner_loser_separation: For each population: % of LOSING episodes with signed_score < 0 (fighting the trend) vs % of WINNING episodes with signed_score > 0 (aligned with the trend). Reported as a 2x2 contingency (win/loss x aligned/fighting/neutral) per population, plus the pooled version.

nulls.shuffle_null: Within each population, shuffle the (episode -> signed_score) label assignment 1000x (fixed seed=1407, same seed convention as S1/TREND-FADE-PREREG for cross-study comparability) holding the P&L values fixed, recompute the bucket-expectancy monotonic-fit statistic (Spearman correlation of bucket vs mean-pnl) each time -- the real (unshuffled) statistic must fall outside the shuffle-null's empirical 90% interval (two-sided, alpha=0.10, same BH-FDR alpha this repo's other pre-regs use) to be considered non-random.
nulls.per_bucket_vs_pooled: Reported BOTH per-bucket (does bucket +3 beat bucket -3 in a direct two-sample comparison) AND pooled (does the whole -3..+3 series show a monotonic-ish trend) -- a population that is only significant pooled but has no clean per-bucket separation is flagged, not silently treated as a pass.

windows.is_oos_split_p1: IS = date < 2026-01-01, OOS = date >= 2026-01-01 (OOS_BOUNDARY, imported verbatim from backtest/autoresearch/strategy_space_grind.py -- same convention as every other T4/T5/P5/trendline study in this repo). Applies to P1 only (P2/P3 are single-era real fills, too small/recent for an IS/OOS split -- reported as single windows).
windows.today_excluded: P2's fetch/cache window ends 2026-07-14 (today, the freeze date) -- any partial/still-open position on the freeze date is excluded from scoring by construction (reconstruct_positions() only returns CLOSED positions with exit_fills present).

statistics.test: Spearman rank correlation of AGREEMENT bucket vs mean per-trade P&L, per population, against the shuffle-null's empirical interval (see nulls.shuffle_null). Two-sample t-test (aligned buckets [+1..+3] pooled vs fighting buckets [-1..-3] pooled) as a secondary, simpler-to-read statistic reported alongside the primary Spearman result -- NOT used to override a Spearman-based verdict, disclosed for readability only.
statistics.evidence_floor: n >= 15 per population for a verdict to be FAIL rather than INCONCLUSIVE-underpowered (OP-16's evidence_n >= 15 advisory floor -- P3 at n=7 is BY CONSTRUCTION always INCONCLUSIVE on its own; P3's ONLY job is corroboration/consistency-check against P1/P2's verdict, never a standalone kill/ship signal).
statistics.concentration_disclosure: top-3-episode % of total population P&L, reported for every population regardless of verdict (OP-20).

kill_criteria_and_confidence_bar.statement: ALL of the following for the hypothesis to be considered SUPPORTED (anything else = KILL, downgraded to INCONCLUSIVE only where n<15 applies per the evidence floor above):
kill_criteria_and_confidence_bar.condition_1_p1_oos_positive_correlation: P1's OOS-only (date>=2026-01-01) Spearman correlation (bucket vs mean-pnl) is positive AND outside the shuffle-null's 90% interval.
kill_criteria_and_confidence_bar.condition_2_monotonic_ish: P1's OOS bucket-expectancy series is monotonic-ish -- defined as: no more than ONE adjacent-bucket inversion across the -3..+3 series (a single noisy dip/spike tolerated, a genuinely flat or sawtooth series is not).
kill_criteria_and_confidence_bar.condition_3_survives_drop_top_3: P1's OOS correlation sign and shuffle-null-beating status are UNCHANGED after dropping the top-3 P&L episodes (per bucket) -- guards against a handful of outlier trades manufacturing the whole result.
kill_criteria_and_confidence_bar.condition_4_both_halves: P1's OOS window split chronologically in half (first-half / second-half, fleet_exit_parity_per_arm.py convention) shows the SAME SIGN of correlation in both halves (does not need to independently clear the shuffle-null in each half, sign-consistency only -- n per half is too small for a stricter bar).
kill_criteria_and_confidence_bar.condition_5_p2_corroborates: P2 (real fills, MEASURED, engine-attributed) shows the SAME SIGN of bucket-vs-pnl correlation as P1's OOS result (even if not itself statistically significant at n~113/8 buckets -- P2's job is directional corroboration on REAL fills, not an independent pass/fail).
kill_criteria_and_confidence_bar.aggregation: 1+2+3+4 are AND, on P1 alone, for P1's OWN verdict. Condition 5 (P2 corroboration) is a SEPARATE, ADDITIONAL requirement for the overall hypothesis verdict to be SUPPORTED -- P1 passing alone with P2 contradicting it is reported as MIXED/INCONCLUSIVE, not SUPPORTED. P3 (n=7) is reported for every condition as color/context but never counted toward pass/fail.
kill_criteria_and_confidence_bar.flat_non_monotonic_is_kill: A flat or non-monotonic P1 OOS bucket series (fails condition_2) is KILL = alignment adds nothing beyond noise -- the SAME 'KILL is a publishable outcome' discipline as every other pre-reg in this program (TREND-FADE-PREREG, TRENDLINE-CONVICTION-OVERRIDE, morning-gate, expected-move-gate). A KILL here means Phase 0's bundle stays LOGGED-ONLY permanently (or is retired) -- it does NOT get promoted to a gate/veto/sizing input.

ship_gate_if_supported: A SUPPORTED verdict does NOT itself change any live behavior (OP-0 #1 / OP-16 eval-first gate). It qualifies Phase 2 -- a NEW, separately pre-registered proposal for HOW the alignment score gets consumed (a soft sizing multiplier? a hard veto on strongly-fighting buckets? informational only, forever?) -- to be drafted and A/B-scorecarded before any params.json change. This pre-reg's scope ends at 'does it correlate', not 'how do we use it'.
no_repick_clause: Once frozen (this commit), no bucket definition, population filter, strike/shape choice (OTM-2/SS-B for P1), attribution convention (P2), seed (1407), FDR/shuffle alpha (0.10), or kill condition may be edited in light of results. A KILL/INCONCLUSIVE across any or all of P1/P2/P3 is a publishable, informative outcome -- not a reason to adjust and re-run. Any genuine build-time correction discovered AFTER this freeze (e.g. a bug in alignment_for_decision) gets fixed via a NEW pre-reg version bump with the correction disclosed, never a silent edit to this frozen spec.

closed_2026_09_02.verdict: KILL. Every population's Spearman correlation between multi-timeframe trend alignment and P&L is NEGATIVE: P1_full rho=-0.025 (n=250), P1_OOS rho=-0.150 (n=90), P2_engine real fills rho=-0.078 (n=386). Kill conditions 1 (OOS positive correlation) and 2 (monotonic-ish) both fail. Alignment is, if anything, mildly ANTI-correlated with outcome -- the opposite of the hypothesis.
closed_2026_09_02.operational_consequence: Gamma_ContextBundle computes exactly this alignment score every 5 min during RTH and its registry row describes a deferred 'Phase 2 (wiring a validated read into conviction/sizing)'. That read is now measured and KILLED, so Phase 2 must not be built. The producer stays logged-only or is retired; either way it is no longer a candidate feature.
